target.name: PvZ 1.0.0.1051 EN (local-engine extracted executable)
target.avz_reference: inc/avz_pvz_struct.h (State @0x28, Hp @0xC8, IsDisappeared @0xEC, AtWave @0x6C) and src/avz_asm.cpp (KillZombie=0x5302F0, RemoveZombie=0x530510)

method: Read-only static disassembly of the locked executable (llvm-objdump 23 from the pinned LLVM-MinGW 20260908 toolchain), cross-referenced with the pinned AvZ framework constants. No game process, no live memory inspection, no hook installed.
protocol_notes: All VA values are absolute addresses in the locked image loaded at 0x400000; RVA = VA - 0x400000.
The AvZ framework independently hard-codes KillZombie=0x5302F0 and RemoveZombie=0x530510; this disassembly is consistent with those entry points.
A byte-pattern scan of the full .text for `movb $1, 0xec(reg)` found exactly one site: 0x530602 inside 0x530510.
No production hook may be implemented from this file alone; the issue's junior gate requires maintainer review of these candidates first.

interception_plan.strategy: MinHook entry hook on 0x530510 (ECX=AZombie*) using the existing register-preserving shim pattern, then copy the full id and classify against the last death-stage fact for the same id.
interception_plan.rationale: 0x530510 is the unique +0xEC writer and every board removal path observed reaches it; entry-only hooking needs no mid-block patch.
interception_plan.abi: ECX(this), plain ret; the shim already saves GPR/EFLAGS/x87/SSE and restores LastError.
interception_plan.board_filter: read board = *(uint32_t*)(zombie+4); require board in the locked image and zombie == pool.block(board+0x90) + (id & 0xffff) * 0x15c with id != 0
rejected_alternatives: hooking 0x530170 for removal (not called on all removal paths)

interception_plan.strategy: Entry+exit hooks on the five State-writing routines: 0x533240 (EAX), 0x532B70 (ECX), 0x5327E0 (EDI), 0x527750 (EAX), 0x52EC00 (EAX + stack flag). Capture State before, re-read State at the epilogue, emit only a change into {1,2,3} for a board-filtered zombie; dedupe per (run, session, full id, stage).
interception_plan.rationale: Each routine already has an idempotence guard and a distinct subtype/phase role; hooking the function boundary avoids patching individual state stores and keeps the ABI adapters small. The aftermath 0x530170 is recorded only as an optional pairing marker, never as the stage fact, because it is absent from variant-a and from 0x533240's remove-only branch.
interception_plan.abi: per-function register argument as listed; reuse the same shim pattern; record the stack flag only for 0x52EC00.
interception_plan.board_filter: same pool-membership check; also require the function's own guard result (State not already dead / not disappeared).
rejected_alternatives: hooking 0x530170 alone as death (misses variant-a and remove-only falling branch)
hooking every raw state-store instruction (five+ sites, no shared ABI)

interception_plan.strategy: Entry hook on the cdecl detach helper 0x530850, filter by caller return address: 0x41BBFF means the recycle sweep free follows, 0x530520 means removal. Record slot/id before the free; verify the free sequence in a fixture.
interception_plan.rationale: The sweep function is shared with plant/grid pools and a mid-block patch at 0x41BBF9 would clobber a push+call sequence; the helper hook is entry-only and the return-address check is ABI-safe.
interception_plan.abi: cdecl: AZombie* is pushed on the stack; at entry [esp] is the caller return address.
interception_plan.board_filter: same pool-membership check plus return-address whitelist {0x41BBFF}.
rejected_alternatives: hooking 0x41BAD0 and filtering by stride (fires for plants/grid items and needs pre-free enumeration)
mid-block MinHook at 0x41BBF9 (6-byte window, higher risk)

residual_questions: Preview/menu objects' +4 field layout was not dynamically verified; the pool-membership filter is the static discriminator.
variant-a (type 29) and variant-b are statically consistent with death animations but were not observed dynamically; a dynamic review must confirm they are not reposition/respawn paths.
No data-driven State writer was found by immediate-value scanning, but computed writes outside the scanned pattern cannot be excluded statically.
Exact semantics of 0x52FE50 (loot/drop housekeeping) and the +0xBA/+0xBD flags are not decoded; they matter for classifying variant-a/b and multi-part deaths.
Attached parts at +0xF4 are separate pool slots and can emit their own State writes; the maintainer must confirm whether one full entity may produce multiple death facts and how to collapse them.
